en: To drive people away so they feel unwelcome or shut out
hook: ALIEN-ATE: makes you feel like an ALIEN.
story: Alienate. To drive people away so they feel unwelcome or shut out. When Arif became class captain, he started giving orders and mocking anyone who made a mistake. Within a month, his friends stopped sitting with him at tiffin time, and he ate alone under the mango tree. He had alienated the very people who voted for him. An alien is an outsider, so to alienate someone is to make them feel like an alien among you. So, what verb means to push people away until they feel shut out? ... Alienate.

gre.s: The senator's harsh remarks about immigrants threatened to ____ the very voters whose support she needed to win reelection.
gre.clue: the very voters whose support she needed

example: The café's sudden price rise alienated the students who had been its most loyal customers for years.

en: Hostile and aggressive; eager to fight
story: Belligerent. Hostile and aggressive; eager to fight. After a small scrape between a bus and a car on Mirpur Road, the car owner jumped out shouting, fists raised, ready to fight the driver and anyone who tried to calm him. Traffic stopped in every direction. A traffic sergeant stepped between them and spoke quietly until the belligerent man finally backed away. Belli comes from the Latin for war, as in rebellion, so a belligerent person is always ready for war. So, what word describes someone hostile and itching for a fight? ... Belligerent.

gre.s: The diplomat's ____ remarks, which included open threats of military action, alarmed even his own government's allies.
gre.clue: open threats of military action

example: After losing the toss, the belligerent captain argued with the umpire so loudly that play was delayed for twenty minutes.

en: Twisted and so complicated that it is hard to follow
hook: CONVOLUTED: like a coiled-up VOLUTE, twisted spiral.
story: Convoluted. Twisted and so complicated it is hard to follow. Joya went to a government office to renew her trade licence. She was sent to room four, then room nine, then back to room four, with a form needing three signatures. By afternoon she sat on a bench, [sigh] holding a pile of papers. The process was hopelessly convoluted. Con means together and volu means roll, as in revolve, so something convoluted is rolled and twisted together like a tangled rope. So, what word describes a process so twisted it is hard to follow? ... Convoluted.

gre.s: Students found the professor's lectures maddeningly ____, as each explanation looped through so many digressions that the main point was lost.
gre.clue: looped through so many digressions

example: The film's convoluted plot, with three timelines and two sets of twins, left most of the audience lost by the interval.

en: Marked by moral decline and excessive self-indulgence
story: Decadent. Marked by moral decline and excessive self-indulgence. In history class, Mahin's teacher described the last years of a once powerful kingdom: rulers feasting through the night and building pleasure gardens while farmers went hungry and every warning was ignored. Mahin was surprised how quickly a great empire could rot from the inside. Historians call such a court decadent. Decadent and decay come from the same Latin root for falling down, and a decadent society is one whose morals are decaying. So, what word describes a society sunk in luxury while its values fall apart? ... Decadent.

gre.s: Moralists of the era denounced the city's nightlife as ____, a sign that luxury and pleasure had corrupted the nation's character.
gre.clue: luxury and pleasure had corrupted the nation's character

example: Critics called the tycoon's gold-plated birthday cake decadent at a time when millions in the country could barely afford rice.

en: To move away from the usual path, plan, or rule
story: Deviate. To move away from the usual path, plan, or rule. For twenty years, Kamal's father took the same road to his office in Motijheel. One morning a burst water pipe flooded the street, and he had to deviate through a narrow lane of old houses. There he found a tiny sweet shop selling the best mishti he had ever tasted. Now he deviates from his route every Friday, [chuckle] just for that shop. Via means road in Latin, so to deviate is to go off the road. So, what verb means to move away from the usual path? ... Deviate.

gre.s: Investigators concluded that the accident occurred because the crew chose to ____ from standard procedures, skipping two of the required safety checks before takeoff.
gre.clue: skipping two of the required safety checks

example: Whenever the professor deviated from her notes, the lecture grew livelier, full of stories from her fieldwork in the haor wetlands.

en: Using dishonest or tricky methods to achieve goals
story: Devious. Using dishonest or tricky methods to achieve goals. During the class election, Rafi noticed something strange. His rival was quietly spreading a rumour that Rafi planned to cancel the annual picnic, which was never true. Nobody saw who started it, but it spread fast, and Rafi felt more hurt than angry. It was a devious trick, clever and dishonest at once. Devious and deviate share the Latin via, road, so a devious person leaves the straight road to get what he wants. So, what word describes someone who uses sneaky, dishonest methods? ... Devious.

gre.s: Unable to win the contract fairly, the company resorted to ____ tactics, secretly leaking false information about its competitors to the press.
gre.clue: secretly leaking false information

example: In a devious move, the company changed its refund policy late on a Friday night, hoping customers would not notice until too late.

en: To spread information or ideas widely
hook: DIS-SEMIN-ate: 'semin' is Latin for seed. Scattering seeds in every direction.
story: Disseminate. To spread information or ideas widely. When a cyclone warning came for the coast near Cox's Bazar, Red Crescent volunteers rode bicycles through the villages with megaphones, while the radio repeated the signal every hour. Mosques announced it, and children ran from house to house. By evening the warning had been disseminated to every family, and people moved into the shelters. Hidden inside disseminate is semin, from the Latin for seed, so to disseminate is to scatter ideas like seeds in every direction. So, what verb means to spread information far and wide? ... Disseminate.

gre.s: Public health officials worked to ____ accurate information about the virus as quickly as rumors were spreading online.
gre.clue: as quickly as rumors were spreading

example: Community radio stations along the coast disseminate cyclone warnings in local dialects so that fishermen understand them quickly.

en: Threats or force used to make someone do something
story: Duress. Threats or force used to make someone do something. A shopkeeper in Narayanganj signed away his land after local thugs visited his shop three nights in a row and warned him about his children. Later, in court, his lawyer argued that the signature meant nothing, because it was given under duress. The judge agreed, and the land was returned to him. Duress shares a root with durable, meaning hard, so duress is hard pressure that leaves you no real choice. So, what word names the threats used to force someone into an act? ... Duress.

gre.s: The judge ruled the confession inadmissible because it had been obtained under ____: the suspect had been threatened and denied sleep for three days.
gre.clue: had been threatened and denied sleep for three days

example: Hostages who praised their captors in a video later explained that they had spoken under duress.

en: Believing in equal rights and opportunities for all people
hook: EGALITARIAN: EGAL means equal in French (égal).
story: Egalitarian. Believing in equal rights and opportunities for all people. At Nadia's grandmother's house in Sylhet, everyone eats together on one long mat: the family, the cook, the gardener, and the boy who brings milk each morning. Nobody gets a better plate, and the youngest serves the oldest first. Nadia once saw a visiting uncle look confused, then [chuckle] sit down happily beside the gardener. Her grandmother's home is truly egalitarian. Egal is French for equal, so egalitarian means believing everyone is equal. So, what word describes the belief that all people deserve equal rights? ... Egalitarian.

gre.s: Although the society claimed to be ____, its rigid caste system ensured that wealth and power remained in the hands of a few families.
gre.clue: its rigid caste system ensured

example: The village cooperative is strikingly egalitarian, giving every member one vote no matter how much land or money they bring.

en: Avoiding giving a clear, straight answer
bn: এড়িয়ে যাওয়া; ধরা দেয় না এমন
story: Evasive. Avoiding giving a clear, straight answer. When Tania asked her younger brother why the window was broken, he talked about the weather, the cricket score, and the strange noise the neighbour's cat made at night. Everything except the window. Tania [laugh] folded her arms and waited. His answers were completely evasive. Finally he [sigh] admitted that the ball had flown farther than he planned. Evasive comes from evade, to slip away, and an evasive answer slips away from the question. So, what word describes an answer that dodges the question? ... Evasive.

gre.s: When asked directly about the missing funds, the treasurer grew ____, changing the subject and answering questions nobody had asked.
gre.clue: changing the subject and answering questions nobody had asked

example: My little brother turns evasive whenever Ammu asks about his homework, suddenly eager to discuss football or the weather.

en: To make something happen faster
hook: EXPEDITE: as fast as an EXPRESS delivery.
story: Expedite. To make something happen faster. Priya's student visa interview was only five days away, but her new passport was still being processed. Her father took the bus to the passport office at dawn, showed the interview letter, and politely asked whether they could expedite the case. The officer nodded and stamped a form, and the passport arrived in two days. Priya [sigh] hugged it with relief. Ex means out and ped means foot, so to expedite is to free the feet so things can move faster. So, what verb means to speed something up? ... Expedite.

gre.s: To ____ the relief effort, the government waived the usual customs inspections for shipments of food and medicine.
gre.clue: waived the usual customs inspections

example: A new online system has expedited passport renewals, cutting the wait from several months to a few weeks.

en: Having or showing intense passion
story: Fervent. Having or showing intense passion. On the night of a big cricket match, Shuvo's grandmother sat right in front of the television, praying under her breath before every single ball. When Bangladesh hit the winning run, she [laugh] clapped and cried at the same time, and hugged everyone in the room. Nobody in the family was a more fervent fan. Fervent comes from the Latin for boiling, so a fervent person's feelings are bubbling hot. So, what word describes passion that is intense and glowing? ... Fervent.

gre.s: Though once a ____ supporter of the policy, attending every rally and writing letters to every newspaper, he became its harshest critic after seeing its effects.
gre.clue: attending every rally and writing letters to every newspaper

example: A fervent believer in public libraries, the retired teacher gave her entire collection of three thousand books to the town of Jashore.

en: Strong, burning enthusiasm or emotion
story: Fervor. Strong, burning enthusiasm or emotion. Before dawn on the twenty-first of February, Lamia joined thousands of people walking barefoot to the Shaheed Minar with flowers in their hands. Old men, schoolchildren and students sang Amar Bhaier Rokte Rangano, their voices rising together in the cold air. Lamia felt the fervor in her chest, a deep passion for the mother tongue that so many had died to protect. Fervor sounds close to fever, and fervor is a fever of strong feeling. So, what word names a burning enthusiasm shared by a whole crowd? ... Fervor.

gre.s: The early ____ of the movement gradually cooled into apathy as its leaders became mired in internal disputes.
gre.clue: gradually cooled into apathy

example: The scientist spoke about coral reefs with such fervor that several students switched their majors to marine biology.

en: Very confident, showy, and colorful in a way that attracts attention
hook: FLAMBOYANT: like FLAMES, bright and impossible to ignore.
story: Flamboyant. Very confident, showy, and colorful in a way that attracts attention. At the Pohela Boishakh fair, Zayan's uncle arrived in a bright red panjabi embroidered with gold, a yellow scarf, and sunglasses shaped like stars. He danced to every dhol, greeted strangers like old friends, and posed for every camera. The children followed him everywhere. He was gloriously flamboyant. Flamboyant comes from the French for flaming, so a flamboyant person blazes like a flame that nobody can ignore. So, what word describes a showy, colorful person who loves attention? ... Flamboyant.

gre.s: Unlike her ____ predecessor, who favored sequined gowns and dramatic entrances, the new director dresses plainly and avoids the spotlight.
gre.clue: who favored sequined gowns and dramatic entrances

example: The flamboyant chess champion arrived at every match in a velvet cape, though his play was cautious and precise.

en: An obstacle; something that blocks progress
story: Impediment. An obstacle; something that blocks progress. Anika dreamed of studying abroad, but her village had no reliable internet, a serious impediment to her GRE preparation. So every Friday she rode a crowded bus for two hours to the district town, where a library had free wifi, and studied until closing time. A year later, she won a scholarship. The impediment had slowed her, never stopped her. Impede comes from the Latin for shackling the feet, so an impediment ties up your feet as you try to move. So, what word names an obstacle that blocks your progress? ... Impediment.

gre.s: Lack of reliable electricity remains the single greatest ____ to industrial growth in the region, deterring investors who might otherwise build factories there.
gre.clue: deterring investors who might otherwise build factories there

example: Poor eyesight was no impediment to Rafiq's career as a radio host, since listeners only ever heard his voice.

en: Designed to start fires; tending to stir up conflict or anger
hook: INCENDIARY: think INCENSE that's lit, or a fire that's lit.
story: Incendiary. Designed to start fires; also, tending to stir up conflict or anger. In a quiet town, someone posted an incendiary message online, a false claim meant to make two neighbourhoods hate each other. Within hours, angry crowds gathered. Then an old imam and a local teacher stood together in the market and calmly told everyone the truth, and the crowd slowly went home. Incendiary words work like incendiary bombs: they are made to start fires. Incense, which is lit to burn, comes from the same Latin root. So, what word describes speech designed to inflame anger? ... Incendiary.

gre.s: The editor refused to print the letter, judging its ____ language likely to provoke riots in an already tense city.
gre.clue: likely to provoke riots

example: The blogger was arrested after posting incendiary videos that urged viewers to attack a neighbouring village.

en: Going on and on without ever stopping
story: Incessant. Going on and on without ever stopping. One July, the monsoon rain over Sylhet fell for three days without a pause. It drummed on the tin roof all night, gurgled in the drains, and turned the lane into a small river. Ishita lay awake, [sigh] listening to the incessant rain, and wondered whether her exam would be cancelled. In means not, and cess comes from the same root as cease, so something incessant does not cease. So, what word describes rain or noise that never stops? ... Incessant.

gre.s: The ____ noise from the construction site, which continued day and night for months, drove many residents to move away.
gre.clue: which continued day and night for months

example: The incessant honking on Mirpur Road makes it almost impossible to hold a phone conversation near the bus stop.

en: Harmless and unlikely to upset anyone
story: Innocuous. Harmless and unlikely to upset anyone. In her first week at a new office in Banani, Sara worried that her question would sound silly in the meeting. Finally, in a soft voice, she asked whether the report could be sent a day later. It was a completely innocuous request, and her manager simply nodded and smiled. Afterwards Sara [laugh] shook her head at herself for being so nervous. Innocuous shares a root with noxious, meaning harmful, and in means not, so innocuous means not harmful at all. So, what word describes a remark or request that harms nobody? ... Innocuous.

gre.s: What seemed an ____ comment about the budget was interpreted by the minister as a direct attack and provoked a furious response.
gre.clue: was interpreted by the minister as a direct attack

example: Most garden spiders are innocuous to humans, though their size frightens many people who find them in the shed.

en: Narrow-minded and uninterested in outside ideas or cultures
hook: INSULAR: like an ISLAND (insula in Latin), cut off from the world.
story: Insular. Narrow-minded and uninterested in outside ideas or cultures. When Farhan went to study in Toronto, he spent his whole first year with other Bangladeshi students, eating at the same Bengali restaurant and never trying anything new. Then a Korean classmate invited him home for dinner, and over bowls of spicy soup Farhan realised how insular his life had become. Insula is Latin for island, so an insular person lives like an island, cut off from new ideas. So, what word describes a narrow mind closed to outside ideas and cultures? ... Insular.

gre.s: Critics accused the academic department of being ____, citing its refusal to engage with scholars from other disciplines or countries.
gre.clue: its refusal to engage with scholars from other disciplines or countries

example: Raised in an insular boarding school, Omar knew almost nothing about popular music until he arrived at university.

en: Fearless and adventurous
story: Intrepid. Fearless and adventurous. Shirin grew up in a crowded Chittagong flat, but every winter she leads a group of young women up the steep jungle trails of Bandarban to the top of Keokradong. They cross slippery streams, sleep in bamboo huts, and climb through the clouds. When others hesitate at a narrow ridge, Shirin goes first, smiling. Her friends call her their intrepid leader. Trepid means trembling, as in trepidation, and in means not, so an intrepid person does not tremble. So, what word describes someone fearless and adventurous? ... Intrepid.

gre.s: The ____ journalist ventured into the war zone that other reporters had fled, sending back dispatches from the front lines.
gre.clue: that other reporters had fled

example: Intrepid divers explored the flooded cave for six hours, mapping tunnels that no person had ever entered.

en: A model of excellence; a perfect example
story: Paragon. A model of excellence; a perfect example. Everyone in Kakoli's village knew Rokeya Apa, the schoolteacher who taught there for forty years. She was never late, never lost her temper, and paid for poor children's books from her own salary. When she retired, the whole village came to say goodbye. She was a paragon of kindness and duty. Paragon comes from an old Italian word for a touchstone, so a paragon is the standard everything else is measured against. So, what word names a perfect model of excellence? ... Paragon.

gre.s: Admired throughout her long career as a ____ of integrity, the judge stunned the public when evidence emerged that she had accepted bribes for years.
gre.clue: Admired throughout her long career

example: Our neighbour, a paragon of patience, taught all six of us children to ride a bicycle without once raising his voice.

en: Having a limited or narrow outlook
hook: PAROCHIAL: limited to the local PARISH.
story: Parochial. Having a limited or narrow outlook. At a neighbourhood committee meeting in Sirajganj, the members argued for two hours about who would pay for one street light, while a flood warning for the whole district lay unread on the table. Imran, a young engineer, finally stood up and reminded them of the river. Their concerns had been painfully parochial. Parochial comes from parish, a small local church area, so a parochial view never looks beyond the parish. So, what word describes a narrow outlook that ignores the bigger picture? ... Parochial.

gre.s: Critics complained that the festival had become increasingly ____, showcasing only local filmmakers and ignoring the vibrant international cinema it had once championed.
gre.clue: showcasing only local filmmakers and ignoring the vibrant international cinema

example: The newspaper's parochial coverage filled its front page with a council quarrel on the very day a war broke out abroad.

en: A strong liking or habitual tendency
hook: PENCHANT: leaning toward it like a PENDANT hangs down.
story: Penchant. A strong liking or habitual tendency. Tanvir's father has a penchant for street food. On every evening walk through Old Dhaka, he stops for fuchka, then a cup of malai tea, then hot jilapi from a pan of bubbling oil. His wife pretends to complain, [chuckle] but she always shares the jilapi. Penchant comes from the French for leaning, from the same Latin root as pendant, so a penchant is something you lean toward again and again. So, what word names a strong, habitual liking for something? ... Penchant.

gre.s: Given the senator's well-known ____ for theatrical gestures, no one was surprised when he tore up the bill on live television.
gre.clue: no one was surprised

example: Kabir's penchant for puns made him popular at parties and unbearable during exam week.

en: Graceful, calm, self-controlled manner
hook: POISE: perfectly POISED, balanced and calm.
story: Poise. A graceful, calm, self-controlled manner. Halfway through Nusrat's speech at the national debate, the microphone died and the hall filled with whispers. She did not panic. She stepped forward, lifted her voice, and finished every sentence calmly, as if nothing had happened. The judges remembered her poise even more than her arguments. Poise also means balance, as when a dancer stands poised on one foot, so think of poise as a mind perfectly balanced. So, what word names a graceful calm that stays steady under pressure? ... Poise.

gre.s: Even when hecklers repeatedly interrupted her speech, the young candidate showed remarkable ____, answering each insult calmly and returning to her argument without missing a beat.
gre.clue: answering each insult calmly

example: Only fourteen, the young pianist played before a packed hall at Shilpakala Academy with the poise of a seasoned professional.

en: To prevent from happening; to make impossible
bn: আগেই রোধ করা; অসম্ভব করে তোলা
hook: PRE-CLUDE: CLOSE the door BEFORE it can happen.
story: Preclude. To prevent from happening; to make impossible. Farhan had trained for months for the inter-university cricket final. Then, three days before the match, he broke his wrist falling off a rickshaw. The injury precluded any chance of playing. He sat in the stands with his arm in a cast, cheering louder than anyone. Pre means before and clude means close, as in include and exclude, so to preclude something is to close the door on it before it can happen. So, what verb means to make something impossible in advance? ... Preclude.

gre.s: The patient's weak heart may ____ surgery, forcing doctors to consider gentler forms of treatment.
gre.clue: forcing doctors to consider gentler forms of treatment

example: Dense fog precluded any flights from leaving Dhaka until midday, stranding hundreds of passengers in the terminal.

en: To fill something up again
story: Replenish. To fill something up again. After a long dry winter, the pond behind Rahima's house in Rangpur had shrunk to a muddy puddle, and the ducks wandered around its edge. Then came the first heavy rains of the monsoon. Within a week the pond was full again, frogs sang at night, and the ducks swam in circles. Rahima [sigh] smiled as the rain replenished it. Plenish comes from the Latin for full, as in plenty, so to replenish is to make full again. So, what verb means to refill something that has run low? ... Replenish.

gre.s: After the long drought, months of heavy rain were needed to ____ the reservoirs, which had shrunk to a tenth of their usual capacity.
gre.clue: which had shrunk to a tenth of their usual capacity

example: Elephants visit the salt lick every evening to replenish the minerals they lose in the summer heat.

en: Strictness, thoroughness, and accuracy; harsh conditions
story: Rigor. Strictness, thoroughness, and accuracy; also, harsh conditions. Before Arif could submit his thesis, his supervisor checked every number, every source, and every comma, and made him repeat one experiment three times. Arif [sigh] grumbled at first. But at his defence, the examiners praised the rigor of his work. The word can also mean harsh conditions, like the rigors of a long winter. Rigor and rigid share a root, so rigor is rigid strictness. So, what word names strict, careful thoroughness? ... Rigor.

gre.s: The journal is famous for its ____: every submitted paper is checked by three independent reviewers, and every statistical claim must be reproduced before publication.
gre.clue: every statistical claim must be reproduced before publication

example: Few of the volunteers were prepared for the rigors of a long winter at the Antarctic research station.

en: Willing to cheat or do wrong to get what one wants
story: Unscrupulous. Willing to cheat or do wrong to get what one wants. A man in a neat suit came to Shuvo's village, promising young men good jobs abroad for a fee of three lakh taka each. Families sold cattle to pay him. Then he vanished, and his phone number stopped working. The police later called him an unscrupulous agent. Scruple comes from the Latin for a small sharp stone, like a pebble in your shoe that troubles you; an unscrupulous person feels no such pebble. So, what word describes someone with no conscience about cheating? ... Unscrupulous.

gre.s: The ____ landlord evicted elderly tenants on false pretexts so that he could rent their apartments at triple the price.
gre.clue: evicted elderly tenants on false pretexts

example: Unscrupulous builders sometimes save money by mixing too much sand into the concrete, endangering everyone who will live inside.

en: Built for practical use, with little thought for beauty
story: Utilitarian. Built for practical use, with little thought for beauty. The flood shelter in Kurigram is a plain grey concrete box on tall pillars, with bare walls, steel shutters and a wide ramp for cattle. It is not pretty. But when the river rose, four hundred people and their animals stayed safe and dry inside. Sometimes a utilitarian building is the most beautiful thing in the village. Utilitarian comes from utility, meaning usefulness: use first, beauty later. So, what word describes something designed purely to be useful? ... Utilitarian.

gre.s: The factory's ____ design, which prioritized efficiency over appearance, made it one of the least attractive buildings in the city.
gre.clue: prioritized efficiency over appearance

example: Grandfather's utilitarian bicycle had no gears, no bell and no paint, yet it carried him to the market for forty years.

en: Fearing or disliking people from other countries
story: Xenophobic. Fearing or disliking people from other countries. When Rafi moved to a small town abroad for his master's degree, a neighbour refused to return his greeting and once told him to go back home. Rafi felt lonely for weeks. But his elderly landlady brought him soup when he caught a cold and introduced him to her friends. One xenophobic neighbour had hurt him; many kind ones helped him heal. Xeno is Greek for stranger and phobia means fear, so xenophobic means afraid of strangers from abroad. So, what word describes fear or dislike of foreigners? ... Xenophobic.

gre.s: Critics warned that the party's ____ rhetoric, which blamed immigrants for every economic problem, would inflame hostility toward the nation's foreign-born residents.
gre.clue: blamed immigrants for every economic problem

example: Some fans shouted xenophobic insults at the visiting team's foreign players, and the league banned them from the stadium for a year.
